title: Happiness
simplified_paragraphs: 一群年轻人到处寻找快乐，但是，却遇到许多烦恼和痛苦。他们问老师苏格拉底：”快乐到底在哪里？”苏格拉底说：”你们还是先帮我造一条船吧！”
年轻人们暂时把寻找快乐的事放到一边，用了49天，造成了一条独木船。他们邀请老师上船，一边划船，一边齐声唱歌。苏格拉底问：”孩子们，你们快乐吗？”学生们回答：”快乐极了！”
苏格拉底说：”快乐就是这样，它往往在你忙着做别的事情时突然来访。”
traditional_paragraphs: 一群年輕人到處尋找快樂，但是，卻遇到許多煩惱和痛苦。他們問老師蘇格拉底：”快樂到底在哪裏？”蘇格拉底說：”你們還是先幫我造一條船吧！”
年輕人們暫時把尋找快樂的事放到一邊，用了49天，造成了一條獨木船。他們邀請老師上船，一邊划船，一邊齊聲唱歌。蘇格拉底問：”孩子們，你們快樂嗎？”學生們回答：”快樂極了！”
蘇格拉底說：”快樂就是這樣，它往往在你忙著做別的事情時突然來訪。”
pinyin_paragraphs: yī qún nián qīng rén dào chù xún zhǎo kuài lè， dàn shì， què yù dào xǔ duō fán nǎo hé tòng kǔ。 tā men wèn lǎo shī Sū gé lā dǐ：” kuài lè dào dǐ zài nǎ lǐ？” Sū gé lā dǐ shuō：” nǐ men hái shi xiān bāng wǒ zào yī tiáo chuán ba！”

nián qīng rén men zàn shí bǎ xún zhǎo kuài lè de shì fàng dào yī biān， yòng le 49 tiān， zào chéng le yī tiáo dú mù chuán。 tā men yāo qǐng lǎo shī shàng chuán， yī biān huá chuán， yī biān qí shēng chàng gē。 Sū gé lā dǐ wèn：” hái zi men， nǐ men kuài lè ma？” xué shēng men huí dá：” kuài lè jí le！”
Sū gé lā dǐ shuō：” kuài lè jiù shì zhè yàng， tā wǎng wǎng zài nǐ máng zhe zuò bié de shì qing shí tū rán lái fǎng。”
english_paragraphs: A group of young people searched everywhere for happiness, but instead they encountered many worries and hardships. They asked their teacher, Socrates, “Where exactly can we find happiness?” Socrates said, “Why don’t you help me build a boat first?”

The young people put their search for happiness aside for the time being. After 49 days, they had made a dugout canoe. They invited their teacher aboard, and as they paddled, they sang together. Socrates asked, “Are you happy, my children?” The students replied, “Very happy!”
Socrates said, “That’s how happiness works. It often comes to visit unexpectedly when you’re busy doing something else.”
english_full:
A group of young people searched everywhere for happiness, but instead they encountered many worries and hardships. They asked their teacher, Socrates, “Where exactly can we find happiness?” Socrates said, “Why don’t you help me build a boat first?”

The young people put their search for happiness aside for the time being. After 49 days, they had made a dugout canoe. They invited their teacher aboard, and as they paddled, they sang together. Socrates asked, “Are you happy, my children?” The students replied, “Very happy!”

Socrates said, “That’s how happiness works. It often comes to visit unexpectedly when you’re busy doing something else.”
